lead.headline: US bars TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL and four others from sponsoring green cards; India calls Vance's 'indentured servants' jibe deeply offensive
lead.byline: INDIAN EXPRESS · TIMES OF INDIA · CNBC · 8–9 OCT
lead.short: Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling suspended Cognizant, Infosys, Capgemini, TCS, Wipro and HCL, and separately Microsoft and Adobe, from the PERM programme, the first step of an employer-sponsored green card; new and pending applications will not be processed. Announcing it, Vice-President JD Vance called H-1B workers brought in by outsourcing firms "indentured servants". On Friday the External Affairs Ministry called the remark "unwarranted" and "deeply offensive".
more: The ministry said the move does not affect existing H-1B visas or the status of holders and their families, though green-card applications of employees at the eight firms could be hit. TCS said its PERM filings were "in single digits" in the last two years and its plans will not change; IT shares rose on Friday.

why.text: The green-card route for Indians at the biggest IT employers is shut for now, and the language from Washington has turned openly hostile.

facts.firms: Cognizant, Infosys, Capgemini, TCS, Wipro, HCL, Microsoft, Adobe

seconds.headline: TCS profit up 15% with AI revenue past 10%; IT leads an 800-point Sensex rebound
seconds.short: TCS made ₹13,884 crore in the September quarter on revenue of ₹73,188 crore, up 11%, and declared a ₹12 dividend (record date 14 October). Annualised AI revenue reached $3.1 billion, more than a tenth of the total. At 13:05 the Sensex was up 806 points at 72,399 and the Nifty at 22,493, with TCS up nearly 4% and ITC leading the gainers.

why.text: The first big IT results of the season came in better than feared, on the same day the US closed the green-card door to the sector.

update.new: Markets recovered most of Thursday's fall, led by IT after TCS's results.
update.front: TCS's results and a sharp rebound together are the day's money news.

seconds.headline: GST Council drops arrest powers, raises the prosecution threshold to ₹5 crore and allows tax credit on staff insurance
seconds.short: The Council recommended deleting the power to arrest under Section 69, prosecuting only cases above ₹5 crore instead of ₹1 crore, cutting the top general penalty from ₹25,000 to ₹10,000 and issuing no show-cause notice below ₹10,000. Companies will be able to claim input tax credit on health and life cover bought for employees. A committee will look at protecting buyers when a supplier defaults. The changes need amendments to the law.

why.text: Group health cover gets cheaper for employers, and small tax disputes stop being criminal ones.

update.new: The Council met and made the recommendations.
update.front: The decisions themselves, including ending arrests for GST offences, are front-page tax news.

seconds.headline: President Murmu meets INDIA bloc leaders tonight; organisers say 10,000 held before Saturday's Delhi protest
seconds.byline: TIMES OF INDIA · SCROLL · HINDUSTAN TIMES · 9 OCT
seconds.short: Rashtrapati Bhavan has given the opposition an 8 pm meeting on its complaints about the Election Commission. The Campaign for Judicial and Electoral Process says at least 10,000 of its members have been detained across the country before its 10 October protest in Delhi. Police have filed 25 FIRs over the protests since 2 October.

why.text: The dispute now reaches the President and the streets of Delhi on the same weekend.

update.new: The President agreed to meet the opposition; mass detentions before Saturday's protest.
update.front: A meeting with the President and a large protest in the capital move the dispute up a level.
